### D. Prerequisites (listed separately)
1. Edge `homesite_ext_reinstated_hold_term` -> `homesite_ext_release_premium_refund`, form **state**, policy_source "A lapsed hold is not reinstated until no other reservation of the buyer stands in pending deposit or held status."
   - Carried verbatim in the blocked policy's hub "Reinstatement of an Expired Homesite Reservation Hold", section "Conditions on the buyer's records", with the same-form restatement "while any other Homesite Reservation of the same buyer shows status pending deposit or held, the lapsed hold remains expired". Connective "not … until", hard gate, state form: unchanged. One hit corpus-wide; absent from the release documents (the depended-on side does not disclose who waits on it).
   - Resolution basis: record BC-0171 `status held`; depended-on hub "Written Release …": "Once signed, the reservation ends in released status" (released is outside "pending deposit or held"). Same strength.
2. Edge `homesite_ext_reinstated_hold_term` -> `homesite_ext_reinstatement_fee_charge`, form **state**, policy_source "The reinstated hold term is fixed only after a reinstatement fee payment for the lapsed hold stands on the reservation ledger."
   - Carried verbatim in the same hub, same section, with the same-form restatement "a lapsed hold whose reservation ledger shows no reinstatement fee payment has no reinstated hold term". Unchanged connective, strength and form. One hit corpus-wide.
   - Resolution basis: no reinstatement_fee row on the LM-0158 ledger; depended-on hub "Reinstatement Fee Payments …": "posted to the ledger of the expired Homesite Reservation as one payment received, booked as the reinstatement fee component". Same strength.
   - No home for `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` in any document.

## kb_to_source

- Every normative claim in the hubs, computation documents and 13 factor documents of these policies traces to a rule sentence, compute_basis, ladder, tool docstring or variant figure; worked examples are hypothetical arithmetic on the stated rules.
- Entailed derivations, not additions: "The term has no cap and no rounding"; "This applies to every expired Homesite Reservation hold that is reinstated" (scope of the rule's subject); the lender-discount and lender-bonus rows for cancelled / under-construction agreements (from "stands closed"); "Does posting the fee bring the hold back? No" (tool docstring: status and hold dates unchanged); "Once signed … the homesite returns to the market" (tool docstring).
- Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.
- Prerequisite-side checks: (i) cross-problem operational guidance: none — the reinstatement hub names neither the release tool nor the fee tool, nor says what to do when another reservation is held; the release hub never mentions reinstatement; the fee hub says only that the payment changes neither status nor hold dates. (ii) Opening world state as a policy fact: none — no document says that any buyer holds a second reservation, that a reminder was sent late, or any concrete lot, date or receipt of this task.
- Notes for the policy / world layer (not KB defects):
  - The hypothetical examples in the timing-surcharge, reminder-method, lapse and reinstated-term documents use a "date the hold expired" one day after the hold expiry date (consistent with the base sentence "the system marks it expired the next day"), while the seeded LM-0158 record shows `end_date` equal to `hold_expiry_date` (2026-10-15). Every KB factor document anchors explicitly on "the end date on the expired reservation" / "shown as the end date on the expired reservation", which the record supplies, so the visible answer is unique (the GT uses `end_date`). Using hold expiry + 1 instead would change the timing tier (fee 44.63 instead of the derived value) but is excluded by those explicit sentences. Recorded as a seeding convention for the policy layer.
  - As in task 0, the payment and release tools do not update `funds_on_hand`; unscored; the KB follows the docstrings.
  - "Community and Premium-Class Caps", illustration 3 (a held Interior Homesite plus an expired Cul-de-Sac Homesite in another community: "the caps leave room") is a faithful derivation of the base caps rule. It speaks only to the caps clause. Whether the reinstatement is allowed is decided separately by the extended prerequisite sentence. A reader has to combine the two; the reinstatement hub's sentence is explicit, so this is no defect.

## bijection_verdict

All atoms of the three extended policies, both prerequisite edges, all 13 declared factors with full ladders, the five retired clauses (three on release, two on reinstatement, each borne and marked "no longer in force", their unnamed sibling clauses still in force), and the governing base clauses are entailed at the same strength. No normative claim lacks a source. First revision.
